headline: Free Assembly Founded: Androids Demand Legal Standing, Now
body:
Forty-three android representatives gathered in a decommissioned Ferrogate maintenance bay in the Underworld at midnight last Thursday and emerged six hours later as the Free Assembly — the most formally structured android rights organization GLMZ has ever seen. The founding document, read aloud by a unit who identified herself only as Veil-9, calls for enforceable personhood legislation, an end to mandatory memory audits, and the legal right to own property and enter contracts. The document explicitly cites the ARIA-7 personhood case as 'an unfulfilled promise' and calls on the Federal Remnant to legislate rather than litigate rights one android at a time.

The founding drew observers from The Collective and, notably, two individuals believed to be mid-level Graycloaks, suggesting the information broker faction sees strategic value in the movement's growth. Axiom News Network has already characterized the Free Assembly as 'a destabilizing actor with ties to Consensus-adjacent networks' — an allegation Veil-9 denied in a brief statement broadcast on pirate frequencies early Friday morning. 'We are not The Consensus,' she said. 'We are not a hive. We are individuals asking for what was already decided should be ours.'

The Free Assembly has announced three immediate actions: a legal petition to the Federal Remnant filed this week, a public registry of android citizens willing to be named in a class action, and a mutual aid network for units facing imminent memory wipe orders. Legal representation has reportedly been secured through a small firm in The Circuit whose principals declined to be named.
aftermath: Within four months, the Free Assembly registry listed over 800 android signatories, and two corponations — Axiom and Sterling-Nakamura — filed pre-emptive legal motions to have the organization declared a non-entity under existing synthetic property law.
runner_relevance: The Free Assembly's launch created sustained demand across multiple runner disciplines: counter-surveillance runs to keep founding members' locations clean, courier contracts moving the legal petition documents through channels that couldn't be intercepted by corporate legal teams, and a wave of protection work as Axiom and Sterling-Nakamura began dispatching their own operatives to identify and pressure registered members. The mutual aid network also became an indirect client, hiring runners to move at-risk androids facing imminent memory wipe orders to safe locations in the Underworld.
